result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.rich_club_coefficient()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the rich-club coefficient for all degree values. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L17242-L17321){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.rich_club_coefficient() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The rich-club coefficient `φ(k)` measures the connectivity among high-degree nodes (the 'rich club' of the network). For each degree `k`, it computes the ratio of actual edges to potential edges among nodes with degree greater than `k`: `\phi(k) = \frac{2E_k}{N_k(N_k - 1)}` where: - `N_k` is the number of nodes with degree > k - `E_k` is the number of edges among those nodes A rich-club coefficient close to `1` indicates that high-degree nodes tend to be connected to each other, forming a 'rich club'. Values less than expected in random graphs suggest the hubs avoid connecting to each other. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping degree `k` to rich-club coefficient `φ(k)`. Only degrees for which at least `2` nodes have degree > `k` are included (otherwise the coefficient is undefined). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - self-loops are ignored in the edge count - edge weights are ignored - for directed graphs, total degree (in + out) is used - returns unnormalized coefficients; for normalized values comparing to random networks, additional computation with degree-preserving random graphs would be needed ## Examples {.doc-examples} Analyze hub connectivity in a network: ::: {#c9f1c684 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a network with clear hub structure graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="hub1") .add_node(label="hub2") .add_node(label="hub3") .add_node(label="spoke1") .add_node(label="spoke2") .add_node(label="spoke3") # Connect hubs to each other (rich club) .add_edge("hub1", "hub2") .add_edge("hub2", "hub3") .add_edge("hub3", "hub1") # Connect spokes to hubs .add_edge("hub1", "spoke1") .add_edge("hub2", "spoke2") .add_edge("hub3", "spoke3") ) rc = graph.rich_club_coefficient() # Returns rich club coefficients dict # Higher values at larger k indicate hubs prefer connecting to each other rc ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {0: 0.4, 2: 1.0, 1: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: Compare with random network: ::: {#98bd20d5 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Scale-free networks often show rich-club phenomenon ba_graph = ec.Graph().add_pa_graph(100, 3) rc = ba_graph.rich_club_coefficient() # Check if high-degree nodes are more interconnected than expected # Filter coefficients > 0.5 to see strong rich-club effect {k: phi for k, phi in rc.items() if phi > 0.5} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {14: 0.5714285714285714, 22: 1.0, 17: 0.8, 20: 1.0, 12: 0.5714285714285714, 23: 1.0, 15: 0.6190476190476191, 18: 1.0, 21: 1.0, 13: 0.5714285714285714, 24: 1.0, 16: 0.8, 19: 1.0} ``` ::: :::
